per_shot.note: Translucent grey box-chain with a few cyan dots; ghostly, no bloom, its light lands on nothing; head is a thin dark crescent that does not read as a threat at play size.
Close-up shows plastic-looking hollow cubes and a pale crescent jaw; washed-out milky water, no self-lighting; body parts muddle into each other.
A single lilac block with a tiny white star under the pod; reads as an ore tile, not a creature; glow barely leaves its cube.
Star-crystal is legible up close and the lilac is a fair accent on CRYOS blue, but it is a flat decal in a cube with no form, no bloom onto neighbours, no threat cue.
Dark teal donut discs in a column, unlit and almost invisible against black rock; no glow, no world colour landing.
Flat 2D teal rings on a dim strip; no facets, no emissive, nothing says pressure or danger.
Riptide is a big black diagonal wedge across the sea-green particle field; reads as a hole in the render, spends black on a non-void thing, no glow.
Same black band dominates; the glowing centipede at top right is the only lit creature and pulls the eye away from the actual hazard.

top_issues.issue: Polyps have no emissive and no form
top_issues.why: They are flat dark teal rings that vanish in the dark; fails glow-that-lands and readable-at-play-size entirely.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Faceted low-poly domes/stalks with a bright sea-green core that blooms and washes the surrounding blocks; brighten the dangerous part.

top_issues.issue: Riptide drawn as a black void wedge
top_issues.why: Black is reserved for true void; a current rendered as a dark slab reads as a rendering gap, not a living hazard of MAELIS.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Render the current as sea-green/nacre luminous flow (swirl, streaming particles) that lights the rock beneath it.

top_issues.why: Translucent grey cubes with no bloom do not separate from the pool; the head/jaw does not read as the dangerous end.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Solid faceted nacre body with emissive seams, a clear open jaw, and a bloom that lights the water surface and pool walls.

top_issues.issue: Frostbloom reads as an ore tile, not a creature
top_issues.why: A lilac cube with a small star decal is indistinguishable from collectables; glow stays inside the cube; no threat silhouette.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give it protruding faceted ice petals/spines that break the block outline, a cold cyan-lilac bloom onto adjacent rock, and a visible armed state.

top_issues.issue: Brinewyrm habitat sits in a cyan CRYOS-looking zone
top_issues.why: Brinewyrm is a MAELIS creature; shown in Heartreach blue-cyan it does not say sea-green/nacre world.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Stage it in a MAELIS brine pool or tint its emissive toward sea-green/nacre.

protect: The sea-green MAELIS particle backdrop and lit pool surfaces in the habitats
Frostbloom's lilac accent against the CRYOS blue is a valid deliberate accent
Pod headlamp beam and visor remain the most legible element in frame

per_shot.note: Faceted crystalline serpent with open jaws and cyan gem studs; bloom lights the water top and reads clearly as a threat at play size.
Strong silhouette, chunky facets, jaw is unmistakably the dangerous end, glow washes the pool surface; head bloom slightly blows out and body is white/cyan rather than nacre-green.
Unchanged from A: lilac tile with a small star under the pod; reads as ore, not a creature.
Unchanged from A: legible star decal, nice accent colour, but flat, glow contained in its cube, no threat cue.
Faceted green domes with bright crystal cores; green bloom spills onto the rock below; readable shapes, though the scene around is very dark and they sit as small bumps at play size.
Chunky low-poly domes, emissive cores, one charging hot-white; light lands on the stone beneath in clear sea-green; danger state is readable.
Sea-green luminous vortex with streaming particles; unmistakably MAELIS, reads as a current hazard, and its light tints the rock and pool.
Swirl fills the whole frame and flattens the dark; the centipede at the top edge competes; still on-palette and readable as a current.

top_issues.why: Identical to A: a lilac cube with a star decal reads as an ore tile, glow does not land, no threat silhouette; it is now the weakest creature in the set by a wide margin.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Faceted ice petals/spines that break the block outline, a cold cyan-lilac bloom washing adjacent blocks, and a visible armed/blooming state.

top_issues.issue: Brinewyrm colour is CRYOS cyan-white, not MAELIS nacre
top_issues.why: Shown in Heartreach (cyan world) with a white/cyan body; it does not say sea-green/nacre, which blurs world identity.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Shift its emissive studs and bloom toward sea-green and add a nacre iridescent sheen, or stage the habitat in a MAELIS pool.

top_issues.why: The vortex's haze fills every pixel, so there is no black left and the hazard boundary is unclear; darkness-as-mechanic weakens.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep the swirl's falloff tighter with a defined edge and let the outer frame return to dark; reduce particle density at the rim.

top_issues.issue: Polyps small and dim at play size
top_issues.why: In the wide frame they read as small bumps in a very dark field; the threat end (core) is bright but the body is low-contrast.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Slightly larger/taller domes or a rim highlight, and a touch more radius on the green light pool so the cluster reads from distance.

top_issues.issue: Brinewyrm head bloom slightly blows out
top_issues.why: The head clips to white at the water line, losing facet detail where the jaw should read.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Cap the head emissive a little and keep facets readable inside the bloom.

protect: Brinewyrm's faceted crystalline body and open jaw silhouette
Polyps' emissive cores and the green light pooling on the stone beneath them, plus the charged hot-white state
Riptide as a luminous sea-green swirl with streaming particles instead of a black band
Pod headlamp beam and visor remain the most legible element in frame

why: B turns three of four creatures (Brinewyrm, Polyps, Riptide) into glowing, faceted, on-palette threats whose light lands; A's versions are flat, unlit or drawn as black void. Frostbloom is identical and weak in both.
